clue.text: Trojan Queen he found on island

parts.note: Cuba is a Caribbean island

explanation.surface: A legendary queen of Troy turns up on a Caribbean island.
explanation.definitionFit: In Homer, King Priam's wife ruled Troy beside him, a mythological queen.

clue.text: Put down about one number over a bet in Australia

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above the next piece
about means the word for put down goes round the next letters

parts.note: to quell a revolt is to put it down
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A punter suppresses doubts about a number before betting in Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: A wager picking the first two finishers in either order is a common Australian racing bet.

clue.text: Blood vessel — vital and prone to get damaged

indicators.note: getting damaged means the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A vital blood vessel is liable to injury.
explanation.definitionFit: This vessel carries blood from the gut to the liver, an important vessel of the body.

clue.text: Judge copy to be a joke

parts.note: to ape is to mimic or copy

explanation.surface: A judge mimics someone for a laugh.
explanation.definitionFit: A prank or playful trick is a light-hearted jest.

clue.text: Audience disapproval swamps the French conductor's finale in Ravel piece

indicators.note: swamps means engulfs, so the jeer wraps round the other letters

parts.note: a boo is the noise an audience makes to disapprove
le is French for the

indicators.note: a finale is the end, so the last letter of conductor is taken

explanation.surface: Booing drowns out the end of a French conductor's performance of Ravel.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravel's best-known orchestral work is this hypnotic, ever-building Spanish dance piece.

clue.text: Cheers about our team in icy venue, turning up in warm clothes?

indicators.note: in means the cheers-and-team piece is placed inside the venue
in a down clue, turning up means the word reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a rink is an ice venue

indicators.note: about means the word for cheers goes round the team

parts.note: ta is British informal thanks
we is our side, us

explanation.surface: Fans cheer their team at an ice rink, turning up in warm clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning up' looks like arriving, but in a down clue it flips the icy venue upwards before the inner piece goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumpers and cardigans made with yarn and needles are woollens worn to keep out the cold.

clue.text: Sustained section of allegretto tune totally recalled

indicators.note: recalled says the hidden letters are read backwards
a section of the phrase is a run of its letters taken from inside it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A musician recalls a whole passage from a light, brisk tune.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Sustained section' as the definition, but 'section of' is what signals the hidden run; the musical term alone means sustained.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian performance direction marks a note held for its full value, so it means sustained.

clue.text: Church expert holding on with note in musical form

indicators.note: holding means the word for expert wraps round the next letters

parts.note: an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A church's resident expert in music is being described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expert' is split after its first letter to hold the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old dance form built on a repeated bass or chord sequence, a recognised musical form.

clue.text: Working one's account towards higher level in gambling centre

indicators.note: in a down clue, moving upwards means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
one's is read as I's, one is

explanation.surface: Someone works their bank account up at a gambling house.
explanation.definitionFit: A building for roulette, cards and slot machines is a hub for gambling.

clue.text: Names borne by followers — Muslims?

indicators.note: borne by means carried inside the word for followers

parts.note: a suite is a retinue of followers
N is short for name, so two of them for names

explanation.surface: Followers carry the names of a faith's members.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the larger branch of Islam are a group of Muslims; the question mark flags definition by example.

clue.text: Stops suspending public relations stunts?

indicators.note: suspending is read as halting or dropping, so these letters are left out

parts.note: to stop something happening is to prevent it

explanation.surface: A company calls off its publicity stunts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspending' looks like hanging, but here it means dropping PR from the word for stops.
explanation.definitionFit: Publicity stunts are staged occasions, so they are examples of happenings; hence the question mark.

clue.text: Fool shortened property boundary

indicators.note: shortened means the last letter is cut off the word for fool

parts.note: a wally is British slang for a silly person

explanation.surface: A foolish neighbour cut back the fence between properties.
explanation.definitionFit: A brick or stone barrier often marks where one plot of land ends and the next begins.

clue.text: Comments with DVD suggesting you avoid Titanic?

definitions.meaning: the booklet of commentary packaged with a recording
read literally, warnings sent to an ocean ship, such as the iceberg messages to the doomed vessel

explanation.surface: Commentary on a film disc might recommend skipping a famous disaster movie.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is a playful one: memos to a big passenger ship, advising it to steer clear.
explanation.definitionFit: The printed commentary inside an album or disc sleeve carries this name, and literally it is messages to an ocean vessel.

clue.text: Cattle disease: skin preset to go flaky

parts.note: rind is the tough skin of fruit or cheese

indicators.note: going flaky means falling apart, so the letters of preset are scrambled

explanation.surface: A cow's skin goes flaky from some illness.
explanation.definitionFit: This viral plague of cattle, now eradicated, devastated herds across Europe, Africa and Asia.

clue.text: Ridiculous description of street guide — little credibility about that

indicators.note: about means the short word for credibility goes round the other piece

parts.note: cred is a shortened form of credibility
an A to Z is the standard British street atlas, so its title is A-Z

explanation.surface: A street map's description is ridiculed for having little credibility.
explanation.walkthrough: The A-Z is a well-known London street atlas.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wild or insane in manner can be described as absurd, a loose synonym.

clue.text: Plans to accept scripture lessons in cathedral

indicators.note: accepting means the word for plans takes the other letters inside

parts.note: charts are maps or plans
RE is religious education, school scripture lessons

explanation.surface: Plans are drawn up for Bible classes held in a cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: The French city is famous for its Gothic cathedral, so the name stands for that building.

clue.text: The marrying kind, swishing endless train around

indicators.note: swishing about suggests movement, so the letters are stirred into a new order
around completes the swishing about, the stirring of the letters
endless means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a train of attendants is a retinue, the followers of a noble

explanation.surface: A bride sweeps up the aisle, her long train swishing round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' suggests a wedding dress, but here it is a retinue of attendants; 'swishing ... around' scrambles RETINU (its letters also read backwards).
explanation.definitionFit: One who joins two things together is what a wedding officiant does, so the marrying kind fits literally.

clue.text: Tropical tree little seen round harbour area? Not entirely

indicators.note: round means the small word wraps round the next piece

parts.note: a tad is a little

indicators.note: not entirely means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a marina is a harbour area for yachts

explanation.surface: A tropical tree is seen near the harbour, though not all of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The tree bears pods whose sour pulp flavours chutneys and sauces, and grows in the tropics.

clue.text: Number expected to seize large lump

indicators.note: seizing means the word for expected grabs the letter inside it

parts.note: due means expected
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A number of people are expected to seize a large lump.
explanation.definitionFit: A small rounded swelling or knot of tissue is a lump.

clue.text: Appear on parade with nothing and lose heart?

parts.note: soldiers fall in when they form up on parade
love means nothing, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A soldier turns up on parade empty-handed and despondent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lose heart' seems to mean despair, but it means giving one's heart away.
explanation.definitionFit: To give one's heart to someone is to be smitten, an idiomatic reading of the definition.

clue.text: Major upset after record congestion

indicators.note: after means the reversed rank goes behind the record

parts.note: a log is a record

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: Maj is the abbreviation for the army rank of Major

explanation.surface: A major upset follows the record congestion.
explanation.definitionFit: A jam of floating timber blocks a river, so the word means a blockage or congestion.

clue.text: Source of coal providing smallest amount of energy?

parts.note: min is short for minimum, the smallest amount
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Coal, a fuel source, yields only a tiny amount of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Coal is dug from a pit, an excavation that is its source.

clue.text: Newcastle area of the country? Not right at first to be nervy

parts.note: NE is the postcode area for Newcastle upon Tyne

indicators.note: not right at first means the leading R, for right, is dropped

parts.note: rural describes the countryside

explanation.surface: A rural area near Newcastle makes someone nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nervy' usually means anxious, but here it is taken literally: to do with nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally, nervy means of the nerves, which is the adjective for the nervous system.

clue.text: Publicly showed stone of archaeological interest?

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, a British weight of fourteen pounds
things that interest archaeologists are very old

explanation.surface: Someone displayed an ancient stone in public.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British unit of weight, 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To put a play or event on before an audience is to present it publicly.

clue.text: Could modify the colour, ultimately? I could

definitions.text: Could modify the colour, ultimately? I could

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: Someone who changes colours of cloth declares they could do it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesperson who changes the colour of cloth is exactly who could modify it.

clue.text: Evening meal: no starter and keep away from the punch

indicators.note: no starter means the first letter is removed, with a menu pun

parts.note: supper is an evening meal
to cut someone is to snub or avoid them

explanation.surface: Skip the first course at dinner and keep off the punch bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' and 'punch' both play on a dinner, but punch is a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer's upward blow to the chin is a specific type of punch.

clue.text: The way lawyers define shelter being shot through by storms

indicators.note: shot through means pierced, so the word for storms goes inside

parts.note: a lee is a sheltered side, out of the wind
gales are storms

explanation.surface: Lawyers describe a shelter battered by storms.
explanation.definitionFit: The dense jargon of legal documents is how lawyers set out their terms.

clue.text: Wrong points announced in speech outlining grammatical structure

indicators.note: announced in speech means the letters are heard, not seen

parts.note: a sin is a moral wrong; tacks are small sharp-pointed nails

explanation.surface: A speaker announces errors in sentence structure.
explanation.definitionFit: The rules for arranging words into sentences make up the grammar of word order.
